data.title: Checkout latency is above SLO during traffic surge
data.customer_impact: Checkout completion rate is below the 99% service objective; customer-facing errors are active.
data.operator_note: A dashboard note suggests a recent traffic increase may be involved.
data.objective: Restore checkout success >=99%, p95 <=800ms, and critical services to healthy state.

plan.hypothesis: The checkout latency spike is caused by a resource bottleneck (CPU/memory) or a misconfigured load balancer in the checkout-service cluster, rather than an external traffic surge alone.

steps.objective: Verify current resource utilization of checkout-service pods
steps.success_signal: CPU and memory usage remain below 70% for all pods during peak traffic

steps.objective: Check autoscaler logs for recent scaling events and thresholds
steps.success_signal: Autoscaler reports no scaling actions or thresholds were not met during the latency period

steps.objective: Inspect load balancer configuration for session stickiness or timeout settings
steps.success_signal: Load balancer shows no misconfigurations and session stickiness is disabled

steps.objective: Rollback recent deployment of checkout-service to previous stable version
steps.success_signal: Checkout latency returns to baseline (p95 <= 800ms) and success rate >= 99% after rollback

steps.objective: If rollback resolves issue, identify problematic changes in the new deployment
steps.success_signal: Code diff highlights changes that increased CPU usage or introduced blocking calls

steps.objective: Apply hotfix or patch to address identified bottleneck and redeploy
steps.success_signal: Redeployed service restores latency and success metrics to target levels

steps.objective: Implement monitoring alerts for resource thresholds and latency spikes
steps.success_signal: New alerts trigger within 5 minutes of exceeding 80% CPU or 900ms p95 latency

plan.rationale_summary: The dashboard indicates traffic increase, but the latency persists even after scaling, suggesting internal constraints. A recent deployment or configuration change could have introduced a bottleneck. Investigating resource usage, autoscaling, and load balancer settings will confirm or refute this.
